findings.summary: Incremental mode still reads all records and audits the full records history, so its cost and work are not limited to what is new.
findings.evidence: Incremental runs still read every intent and landing via ls_tree_under/cat_blobs and still run records_branch::audit_history over the whole records history (the open question keeps it a full audit). docs/design/records-history.md §9 (lines 357-358, 371-372) says cost must depend on new commits and 'incremental time must not scale with the 4,000 old records'. Under this plan, records_judged is only a counter of new records. Fix: In incremental mode, audit records history only from checkpoint.records_sha to the tip. Parse only the records added since records_sha (diff-tree), and look up the older intents those new landings cite by id or path instead of loading every record. Add a fixture assertion that the incremental run parses only new records plus the intents they cite.
findings.location: Plan decision 2, open question 2; crates/athena-gate/src/attribution.rs:220 (audit_history), :152 read_records

findings.summary: CI=true implies read-only, so binary write tests would fail when cargo test runs in CI.
findings.evidence: The CI workflow runs cargo test with CI set. Binary tests that expect a passing check or land to write a checkpoint would see no write. Fix: Have every binary test that expects a write call env_remove("CI"), and set CI explicitly only in the read-only case.

findings.summary: The plan does not say how the newest checkpoint is chosen.
findings.evidence: Checkpoint.created_at is self-reported (history.rs:290), so a forged later timestamp could win. Fix: Choose the newest checkpoint by records-branch commit order, not by created_at, and document this.

findings.summary: The plan conflates an incremental fallback with a replay disagreement.
findings.evidence: When the checkpoint's records_sha is not an ancestor, the plan both falls back to full replay and adds a CheckpointDisagrees finding. Fix: In incremental runs, report a non-ancestor records_sha as a replay_reason, and keep CheckpointDisagrees for full-replay mismatches only, or document why both apply.

summary: I checked the plan's references against the snapshot. The Checkpoint record exists with main_sha, records_sha and verifier_version (history.rs:286). check_attribution and walk exist (attribution.rs:181, :189). The CI attribution job exists with contents: read (ci.yml:18-19, 178-195). The demonstrations for the tamper, version-change and write/no-write criteria would each fail without the behavior. The main problem is the design of incremental mode: it still loads every record and audits the whole records history on every run. Its records_judged count would therefore be cosmetic, and incremental cost would still grow with total history, which contradicts §9 of the design doc and the point of the measurement. Smaller issues: the CI environment variable would break the write tests when they run in CI, and the plan does not say how the newest checkpoint is chosen. Revise.
